what: Paths of the subject repository removed from the work tree for arms A, B and C (plan 34 §4: 'GQ の指示ファイルを除いた木'). Arm D removes nothing. Patterns are matched against the tracked paths of the pre-fix commit: a trailing '/' is a directory prefix, '**/NAME' is a file of that name at any depth, anything else is an exact path. The paths actually removed are recorded per task (local) and counted in the G4 result.
status: REVIEWED: docs/planning/34-review-g5.md 11.B1 (2026-11-13). remove = the plan's five + AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .claudeignore, .geminiignore; .husky/ stays in every arm. The same patterns are removed from EVERY commit of the history given to arms A, B and C (owner decision 2026-11-13 05:0x).

remove.rationale: Named by the plan (CLAUDE.md, every level). Claude Code loads the root file at start and the nested ones when it works in their directory.

Named by the plan: skills, agents, hooks, settings.json. Removing settings.json also removes the hooks and the permission rules, which is why arm D can differ from A/B/C in permissions (review §10.5 item 4).
Named by the plan. The role and process documents the .claude agents point to.
Named by the plan. Instruction file of another agent with the same rules.
Named by the plan. A generated knowledge graph that the harness tells the agent to query before grep. Absent at commits where it is git-ignored.
NOT in the plan's list. Found at the root when the first tree was built. A Claude Code configuration file (which paths the agent does not read); part of the harness by function. Proposed: remove.

NOT in the plan's list. Same function as CLAUDE.md for other agents (present at the root). Claude Code does not load it by itself, but an agent that lists the root sees it and can read the rules. Proposed: remove, otherwise A is not 'told nothing'.
NOT in the plan's list. Present at the root and next to every nested CLAUDE.md (docs, infra, src/routes, tests, .github). Same reasoning as AGENTS.md.
NOT in the plan's list. Harmless either way; removed with GEMINI.md for consistency.

keep_but_flagged.rationale: Review 11.B1: kept in all arms. Not an instruction file but a project tool, like the CI definitions; the hooks are installed in no arm (npm ci --ignore-scripts).

ADRs. Several are process rules for agents and reviewers (quality gates, review standards), others are product and technical decisions a developer needs. Kept: they are the project's documentation, not the harness. A reviewer may want the process ADRs removed; that needs a per-file list.
Project design documents. Kept. Note: some sections are addressed to 'AI agents' and restate harness rules.
Human-facing process documents and templates. Kept. They describe the PR checklist; no PR is opened in this experiment.
CI definitions. Kept: they are how a developer learns what the project checks.

The project's own check scripts. Kept: they are the project's tools. Many of them, and about 67 test files, read the removed paths and so fail after removal (counted in G4, listed in the task's environment facts).

keep_but_flagged.pattern: tests/** and scripts/__tests__/** that name removed paths
keep_but_flagged.rationale: Kept and left red, reported as environment facts (plan 34 §4). The alternative, deleting those tests in A/B/C, would hide that the tree was altered and changes Q2.

also_removed.what: git remote, tags, other branches, and every object after the pre-fix commit
also_removed.rationale: Owner decision 2026-11-13: every arm gets the history up to the pre-fix commit. A/B/C get it from a mirror in which the patterns above are filtered out of every commit; D gets the real history. The task repository is a fresh fetch of one commit, so nothing later is in its object store (checked in the image).
